saw_lines: Parents buy a child’s bed or sleeping bag once, then research safety, fit and delivery for weeks before they pay.
So the ad has to answer delivery, safety and price in its first lines, or the parent leaves to compare.
Your 6 ads with written copy carry no proof number, so a new parent has nothing to trust before clicking. Open the next batch with a review count or orders shipped.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 27 Oct 2026
points: 0 of your 6 ads with written copy carry a proof number, so a parent comparing safe beds has nothing concrete to trust before clicking. Collect one figure, a review count or orders shipped, and open the next batch with it.

12 of your 18 ads are catalog feed ads with no story, so a scrolling parent has no reason to stop. Add three story ads opening on one problem, like a toddler climbing out at night, each linked to its product.

13 ads have run 60 days or more, so they are the copy to build from. Build three more variations of your oldest winner, changing only the opening line and the product shown, so the proven structure carries into new tests.

All 18 ads say Shop now yet send buyers to 10 different pages, so the label promises nothing about where they land. Match each button to its page, such as Shop beds for bed ads and Shop shoes for shoe ads.
